notes.blurb: White quartz under a gilded copper roof, banded in purple: the brightest and richest palette this project has, for the quarter at a place's centre and never for the whole of an ordinary one.
notes.construction: Dressed quartz ashlar on a pale diorite footing, birch posts and lintels framing tall openings, purpur string courses at sill and cornice; the second stone is cherry, a rose-tinted wall for the houses between the white ones.
notes.ground: Smooth quartz paving, swept and laid flat; the ground of a ceremonial quarter is made rather than planted.
notes.roofs: Copper tile over two pitches, steep at the ridge and easing out to an upturned eave, hipped and gabled together at the ends; the civic halls carry the same tile in two tiers.
notes.signature: A gilded roof on a white wall with a purple band under the eave, so the richest ring of a place reads from the air as the one bright thing in it.
